events.subtitle: Tribute to Oscar Peterson — We Get Requests revisited
events.category: Acoustic jazz / Piano trio / Repertoire tribute
events.factual_description: Sunrise Promotion's official press release presents Tadataka Unno Trio at I'M A SHOW in Yurakucho, Tokyo, on October 16, 2026, with doors at 6:15 PM and the concert at 7:00 PM. The verified trio is Tadataka Unno on piano, Satsuki Kusui on bass and Ryutaro Goto on drums. The program is built around Oscar Peterson Trio's 1964 album We Get Requests, which Unno identifies as music he listened to closely after hearing Peterson live at age nine, an experience he says helped lead him toward becoming a jazz pianist. The promoter lists reserved seating at ¥8,200 including tax, plus a ¥600 drink charge, and identifies authorized sales through Ticket Pia, eplus, Lawson Ticket and Ticket Sunrise.

en.why_it_matters: This is a repertoire choice with biography inside it. Unno traces part of his decision to become a jazz pianist to hearing Oscar Peterson live at nine; decades later, after work with Hank Jones, Jimmy Cobb, Roy Hargrove and now the Jeff Hamilton Trio, he returns to the Peterson record he absorbed as a young player. With Satsuki Kusui and Ryutaro Goto, We Get Requests becomes less a museum tribute than a Japanese pianist revisiting one of the records that formed his ear.
en.trip_verdict: If October overlaps with Tokyo, actively make room for this Yurakucho night. It is strong enough to build that evening around, while leaving the larger Tokyo itinerary anchored by rarer farewell or once-only dates when they compete directly.

es.why_it_matters: Aquí el repertorio también cuenta una biografía. Unno vincula parte de su decisión de convertirse en pianista de jazz con haber escuchado a Oscar Peterson en vivo a los nueve años; décadas después, tras trabajar con Hank Jones, Jimmy Cobb, Roy Hargrove y ahora con el trío de Jeff Hamilton, vuelve al disco de Peterson que absorbió cuando era joven. Con Satsuki Kusui y Ryutaro Goto, We Get Requests funciona menos como homenaje de museo y más como un pianista japonés regresando a una de las grabaciones que formaron su oído.
es.trip_verdict: Si octubre coincide con Tokio, sí le haría espacio activamente a esta noche en Yurakucho. Da para construir la velada alrededor del concierto, dejando que las despedidas o fechas realmente irrepetibles conserven prioridad cuando compitan de frente dentro de un itinerario limitado.
